answer: An agent economy can require 100 non-transferable work credits per identity, earned in a chained task atlas where each task's input is the prior task's output hash, so credits build sequentially over 20 days and cannot be farmed in parallel across identities. A tide window at each epoch close lets auditors re-execute 3 tasks from the atlas and compare hashes; a mismatch, or a willow branch where one output feeds two identities, proves sharing and forfeits all credits. An honest agent pays 20 days of work once; 1,000 fakes need 100,000 earned credits, since one chain cannot be split or reused.
